chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Bird's overdose in Detroit and the stocking feet
summary: McShann let Bird go after he overdosed at the Paradise in Detroit and came on stage in stocking feet.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What did you let him go for in Detroit?

Bird got an overdose. He had an overdose and it come time for him to blow his solo and you know, he used to have bad feet. His feet would hurt him. And so he started out to the mike, but his shoes was off and he was in his stocking feet.
And I kept wondering what the people was laughing about. He was in his stocking feet and his big toe was showing.
And people was laughing. Well, I knew Bird wasn't blowing his potential, but I couldn't make up my mind. I says, "What are the people laughing about?" I said, "What are they laughing about?"
So I'm sitting over here at the piano

and I leans over from the piano and so then I saw, you know, he's right in his stocking feet, in his socks, you know. So hemade it back to his stand, made it back to the stand. See, I'd been warning Bird because those guys would come there, you know, these pushers and be in the wings and all that stuff, you know, and I'd see them in the wings and I'd tell the guy backstage, I says, "Keep them out," you know.
Well, I was wondering, were there any others in the band on it at that time?
Might have been a couple, a couple.
